## Jaccard similarity measures between genome based on the accesory gene abundance, can also use the method available in `vegan`, the default is bray-curtis. (0 value
represents the closest genomes)

```{r distance_genome}

jacc_dist_acc <- pagoo_rssc$dist(method = "jaccard", binary = T) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>%
  pheatmap::pheatmap(main = "Pairwise similarity between genomes",

                     show_rownames = F,
                    height = 15)
```

# Estimate pangenome size with micropan, according to the theory the pan-genome 
is closed if the estimated `alpha` is above 1.0

```{r , eval=F}
library(micropan)
# pa <- read_csv(rssc_sens_pacsv) %>% 
  
get_heaps <- function(path_rtab, iter=500){
  
  # read the data from path; column should be genes and rows are genomes
  pa = readr::read_tsv(path_rtab, show_col_types = F) %>% 
    column_to_rownames("Gene") %>% 
    t() %>% 
    as.matrix()
  
  # pass to micropan heap
  if (iter < 500) {
    print("Warning! No of iteration should be > 500. Will run it with n.perm=500")
    # iter <- 500
    
    alphaa <- micropan::heaps(pa)
    chao <- micropan::chao(pa)
    
    stats <- list(alpha = alphaa[[2]], chao = chao)
  }else{
    
    alphaa <- micropan::heaps(pa, n.perm = iter)
    chao <- micropan::chao(pa)
    stats <- list(alpha = alphaa[[2]], chao = chao)
  }
  # second elem is alpha 
  return(stats)
}

# calculate heaps; takes 5 mins
heaps_est <- list(rssc = "<PROJECT_ROOT>/Results/Pangenome/PANAROO/RSSC-sensitive/gene_presence_absence.Rtab") %>%
  map(.x = ., .f = ~ get_heaps(path_rtab = .))
#      ralstonia = "<PROJECT_ROOT>/Results/Pangenome/PANAROO/Ralstonia_159_GenBank-sensitive/gene_presence_absence.Rtab") %>%
#   map(.x, .f = ~ get_heaps(path_rtab = .))


heap_est <- as.data.frame(list(param = c("alpha", "chao"),
                   rssc = as.double(heaps_est$rssc))
              )

# write as a table
heap_est %>% 
  write_csv(., 
            file = "<PROJECT_ROOT>/Notebooks/Heaps_estimation.csv")

```


## Rarefraction/Pangenome accumulation curve
- Pagoo applies power-law distribution to fit the pangenome size and
- exponential decay function for fitting the core genome size.

```{r pangenome_accu}

rarefrac <- pagoo_rssc$gg_curves(size = 2) +
  # ggtitle("Pangenome accumulation/rarefraction curves") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 2) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.3, 0.4),
        legend.justification = c("left", "top")) +
  scale_color_aaas() +
  annotate("text", 
           label = paste0("alpha: ",
                                  round(heaps_est$rssc$alpha, digits = 3)),
           x = 25, y = 16000) +
  
  annotate("text",
           label = paste0("chao: ", 
                          round(heaps_est$rssc$chao, digits = 3)), 
           x = 25, y = 15000)


genome_vs_genes <- pagoo_rssc$gg_barplot() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  ylab("")
  


# ggpubr::ggarrange(rarefrac, genome_vs_genes, ncol = 2)
rarefrac + genome_vs_genes


```

```{r}

panstripe.accumulation <- function(pa, nperm=100){
  
  if (!is.list(pa)){
    pa <- list(pangenome=pa)
  }
  
  plotdf <- purrr::imap_dfr(pa, ~{
    .x <- t(.x)
    purrr::map_dfr(1:nperm, function(i){
      ppa <- .x[sample(nrow(.x), replace = FALSE), sample(ncol(.x), replace = FALSE)]
      cumlative <- rowSums(apply(ppa, 1, cumsum)>0)
      cumlative <- cumlative-cumlative[[1]]
      df <- tibble::tibble(N = 1:length(cumlative),
                           naccessory = cumlative,
                           permutation = i)
      return(df)
    }) %>%
      tibble::add_column(pangenome=.y)
  })
  
  plotdf <- plotdf %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data$N,.data$pangenome) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      `accessory size` = mean(.data$naccessory),
      `std` = stats::sd(.data$naccessory))
  
  
  return(plotdf)
}
  
  

panstripe.accumulation(pa = as.matrix(rssc_sens_pa))

```
